evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1), against the Xerces-C of the OpenMS4 Linux x86_64 Release build, configured as Internal::XMLFile::parse configures it
method: Wave-4 integration found three SAX drivers written by three lanes (F6 format/sax_xml.rs, F3b format/search_engine_xml.rs, F3a format/xml_sax.rs), each delivering character data differently. An oracle driver (../oracle/integ-F-xerces-sax/driver.cpp) creates the SAX2XMLReader exactly as FORMAT/XMLFile.cpp does (namespaces and namespace prefixes off), links the Release install /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/opt/openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 and its Xerces-C with conda-forge g++ 14.4.0 and libOpenMS's core flags, and records every startElement, endElement and characters callback (with its UTF-16 length) and every fatal error with its line for 28 documents; it ran twice on ibminode06 with identical output. The result: Xerces splits character data at every reference (the text before it is one callback, the replacement starts the next), ends a run at a comment or processing instruction, delivers a CDATA section (even an empty one) as its own callback, and reports NUL character references, an upper-case X radix, a literal < in an attribute value and the usual well-formedness errors as fatal errors on the line the scanner stands on. None of the three drivers matched; the one remaining driver, src/format/sax_xml.rs, replays all 28 cases in its release_callbacks unit test (locator columns are not compared; the internal-DTD case and ISO-8859-1 in UTF-8 mode are refused as documented native differences).
